newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Ex-Soviet states plan regional Interpol bureau.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet states plan regional Interpol bureau.

text.p: Former Soviet republics agreed on Thursday to step up cooperation to fight rampant organised crime by establishing a joint Interpol bureau for the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

The head of Russia's Interpol office, General Ivan Sardak, told CIS interior ministers in the Moldovan capital Chisinau this would strengthen their hand with West European police, whom he accused of not doing enough to combat the smuggling of stolen cars into Eastern Europe and passing the buck to their CIS counterparts.
Governments will be asked later this year to approve the plan for a joint Interpol bureau.
"Such a bureau will allow existing material and databases to be used more effectively to combat organised crime," Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov told the meeting.
The 12 CIS members have their own national offices of Interpol, the cross-border police coordinating body.

Interpol's secretariat, worried about cross-border crime from the former Soviet Union, proposed that a regional CIS bureau should be set up. It will be equipped free by Interpol. Russia has suggested siting the bureau in Moscow.
Sardak told the meeting: "The world community still views the CIS as a single criminal space. A regional CIS Interpol bureau will help to get rid of organisational confusion."
It would also give former Soviet states more clout internationally, he said.
"We could talk on equal terms with organisations like Europol (the European Union police agency)," Sardak said. "We have to defend our regional interests."
The CIS groups all the former Soviet republics except the three Baltic republics -- Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
